impactStory.heading: A place where life happens.
impactStory.lede: Four stories from a congregation that already is a family, and shows up for the city around it. The building we are raising makes room for all of it.

family.title: One family. Together for what is right.
family.body: Four thousand members, forty nationalities, one community. We stand together, in prayer and in learning, in joy and in grief, with each other and with our neighbours. To belong here is to belong to something larger than yourself.

learning.title: Lectures, conversations, and teaching.
learning.body: Evening talks on mental health, Quran classes for children, Arabic for beginners, calligraphy, philosophy. Nineteen teachers, four hundred pupils, waiting lists in every class. What is said here stays with you.

volunteer.title: We show up, for each other and for the city.
volunteer.body: Volunteers in yellow vests hand out meals, coordinate with the district, and stand with neighbours in good times and hard ones. Rabita isn't only a place you come to. It's a place you come from, to help.

sadaqa.title: Sadaqa jariya, a gift that lasts.
sadaqa.body: The prayer rug is perhaps the most-used object in the mosque. Each place in the new hall can be given in the name of someone we've lost. The names stand as long as the building stands.

statement.before: Oslo's first mosque belonging to no single nationality.
statement.accent: Now we are making room for everyone it brought together.

buildingRises.heading: From foundation to prayer hall.
buildingRises.lede: Scroll to see the building take shape, seven floors above and below the street, each with its purpose. Every kroner builds a layer.

intro.body: The old mosque was demolished during Ramadan 2025. Seven floors are to go up. Scroll to watch them arrive.

building.title: Seven floors on one address.
building.lede: A mosque, a school, a library, a kitchen and a hall, stacked on the plot at Calmeyers gate 8. Two floors below the street, five above it.
building.brief: The old mosque was demolished in 2025. What replaces it is one building doing the work of five, on a 6 762 square metre plot, designed so the ground floor stays open to the street rather than turning its back on it.

items.title: Prayer halls
items.body: Room for 500 women and 2 000 men across three floors, against 100 places for women today.

items.title: The school
items.body: The largest Arabic school in Norway, 400 pupils and 19 teachers, in daylight classrooms.

items.title: Library and youth

items.title: Entrance and cafe

money.title: Costed room by room.
money.lede: Every krone is tied to something physical in the building, and the accounts that prove it are public.
money.brief: The campaign is 100 million kroner across three phases. 26 995 179 kroner is in, which is 26 per cent, and the phase it belongs to is stated rather than implied. Rental apartments are part of the building specifically so maintenance never consumes the organisation again.

visit.heading: Coming in person.
visit.body: The door is open every day. You do not need to be a member, and you do not need to book unless you are bringing a group.

times.title: Five prayers, every day of the week.
times.lede: Times are calculated for Oslo and change with the season. Friday prayer is the fixed point in the week, and the hall fills long before the khutba.

Night prayer, the last of the five.
Friday prayer, with the khutba before it.

services.title: Nikah, janaza, shahada and counselling.

rows.detail: The marriage ceremony, held in the hall or in a smaller room.
Funeral prayer and help with the practical steps that follow.
The declaration of faith, taken with an imam and witnessed.
A conversation with an imam, in confidence, about whatever it is.
Classes and university groups are welcome to sit down and ask.

cards.title: Come and ask
cards.body: Reception is open the same hours as the building. For most things a conversation is enough to get started.

cards.title: Send it in writing
cards.body: For a funeral or anything time sensitive, write or ring. Somebody answers the same day.

whereMoneyGoes.heading: Every krone is accounted for.
whereMoneyGoes.runningCost: The old mosque consumed most of the organisation's resources in maintenance. Rental apartments are part of the new building specifically so that never happens again.

privacyPage.title: Short and simple.
privacyPage.lede: We collect as little as possible, store it securely, and build the site so it works for everyone.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.controller: The data controller is Rabita, org.nr. {orgNr}, at Calmeyers gate 8, Oslo.
privacy.dataWeCollect: We store name, email, phone number and donation details to process gifts and tax deductions. Site analytics are anonymous.
privacy.fnr: National identity number is collected only where you opt in for tax deduction. It is encrypted at rest, access-restricted, and deleted after the statutory period.
privacy.hosting: The site is hosted in the EEA. We do not use third-party tracking before you consent.
privacy.rights: You have the right to access, rectify and delete. Write to us and we reply within 30 days.

a11y.heading: Universal design
a11y.wcag: We build to WCAG 2.1 AA. Where anything falls short, write to us. We fix on a rolling basis.

list.contrast: Colour contrast is tested, with particular attention to the gold accent.
list.keyboard: All functionality is keyboard-operable, including the giving sheet (Escape closes).
list.textsize: Text size controls at the top of every page, remembered on your device.
list.rtl: The site is built with logical properties, so right-to-left for Arabic works naturally.
list.altText: Images and illustrations have alt text; pure decoration is hidden from screen readers.

a11y.feedback: Feedback? Write to us. We prioritise all accessibility reports.

servicesIndex.lede: We provide religious services to members and to others who wish. All enquiries are handled discreetly.

nikah.title: Nikah: wedding ceremony
nikah.body: Islamic marriage, with or without legal registration.
nikah.longBody: We host nikah both at the mosque and elsewhere by arrangement. Witnesses and imam are coordinated. Legal registration is handled through the Norwegian civil registry; we help with the formalities.

janaza.title: Janaza: funeral
janaza.body: Washing, prayer and coordination with the cemetery.
janaza.longBody: The janaza service is available 24 hours. We help with practical arrangements with Alfaset cemetery and other burial grounds in Oslo. No cost for members.

shahada.title: Shahada: declaration of faith
shahada.body: For those who wish to take shahada, with witnesses.
shahada.longBody: We host both private and public shahada ceremonies. Get in touch to arrange a time. We provide witnesses if needed and offer brief guidance afterwards.

counselling.title: Counselling and conversations
counselling.body: Confidential conversations with an imam or female counsellor.
counselling.longBody: We offer both short and longer conversations, individually or as a couple. All enquiries are confidential. We can offer both a male imam and a female counsellor.

hajj-umrah.title: Hajj and umrah
hajj-umrah.longBody: Rabita does not organise trips itself, but we help with preparation, information and referrals to experienced agencies and imams accompanying groups.

aboutPage.title: Rabita since 1987.
aboutPage.lede: From a flat in Grønland to one of the largest and oldest mosques in Norway.

history.p1: Rabita was founded in 1987 as the first mosque in Oslo not tied to a single nationality. The idea was simple: a place for Muslims in Norway, regardless of where they came from.
history.p2: The congregation grew, the school was established, and the cultural centre became part of civil society in Oslo. The old building ran out of space long ago.
history.p3: In October {year} King Harald V and Crown Prince Haakon visited the mosque, the first royal visit to a mosque in Norway. We continue to work with the same aim: a place where faith and civic life belong together.

board.heading: The board
board.body: The board is elected by members at the AGM. Full names of each board member are published after the next AGM.

contactPage.title: Write to us.
contactPage.lede: Gifts, membership, services or press. We reply within 3 working days.
contactPage.note: For urgent matters (janaza), please call reception.

volunteerPage.title: Help run Rabita.
volunteerPage.lede: We need volunteers for events, teaching, the library and much more. No commitment until you and we agree on what fits.

teaching.title: Arabic, Qur'an, and a school week that fits around the Norwegian one.
teaching.lede: Four hundred pupils and nineteen teachers, running every week of term. The new building gives the school its own floor instead of the rooms it borrows now.
teaching.caption: A Qur'an on the rehal at Rabita

close.heading: Enrolling a child.
close.body: Places are grouped by level rather than by age, so a child who has never read Arabic sits with others starting in the same place.

items.detail: Autumn and spring, following the Oslo school calendar.
From six years old, in groups by reading level.
Set per term, and no child is turned away over it.

visit.title: Come and see the place.
visit.lede: School classes, university groups, neighbours and anybody curious. You do not need a reason and you do not need to be Muslim.
visit.caption: The square outside during Ramadan

facts.detail: Gronland, a few minutes from the station

visit.closeBody: If you are bringing a group, tell us roughly how many and when. Everything else can be sorted on the day.

events.title: Eid, iftar, lectures and family days.
events.lede: The year has a rhythm. Ramadan fills the street outside, Eid fills the hall, and the rest of the year runs on lectures, courses and the days families turn up for.
events.caption: Street iftar outside the mosque, Ramadan 2025

facts.detail: Iftar, Eid, lectures and family days
Free unless the listing says otherwise

events.closeBody: The street iftar is the easiest way in. Tables go up outside, food is free, and nobody asks who you are.

about.title: Founded in 1987, and still on the same street.
about.lede: Det Islamske Forbundet has been in Gronland since the eighties. The congregation outgrew the building a long time ago, which is the whole reason for the build.
about.caption: The new facade at night, Norconsult

news.title: What is happening, told plainly.
news.lede: Notices from the congregation and progress on the build. No press releases, just what changed and when.
news.caption: Ramadan on the street outside, 2025

membership.title: Becoming a member.
membership.lede: Membership is how the congregation counts itself and how the state grant is calculated. It also decides who votes at the annual meeting.
membership.caption: A gathering at Rabita

volunteer.title: Where hands are needed.
volunteer.lede: Iftar does not cook itself and the school does not run on teachers alone. Tell us what you can do and roughly when.
volunteer.caption: Volunteers during Ramadan

contact.title: Call, write, or come by.
contact.lede: Reception is open the same hours as the building. For anything time sensitive, ring rather than write.
contact.caption: A conversation over tea at Rabita

colophon.heading: For the record.
colophon.body: The details a member, a journalist or an auditor might want to check, kept in one place.
